findings.summary: Amiga is a family of personal computers produced by Commodore from 1985 until 1994, notable for custom hardware that accelerated graphics and sound. It established a niche in audio and multimedia, becoming a popular platform for music creation and video production. The system's custom chips enabled sprite graphics, blitting, and four channels of sample-based audio, supporting a desktop GUI and pre-emptive multitasking via AmigaOS. While initially slow to sell, the Amiga 500 became the bestselling model, finding success in gaming and creative software before market share declined against IBM PC compatibles and fourth-generation consoles, leading to Commodore's bankruptcy.

mechanisms.title: Custom audio hardware
mechanisms.explanation: The Amiga featured four channels of sample-based audio custom hardware, which distinguished it from contemporaries and supported its emergence as a platform for music creation and trackers.

mechanisms.title: Custom graphics and blitter
mechanisms.explanation: Custom hardware including sprites and a blitter accelerated graphics performance, enabling the system's success in video games and multimedia authoring tools.
